title: Efficacy of Digital Lending Platforms on Debt Management Behavior Among Young Professionals in Davao City
authors: Esperanza, K.; Belaca, A.; Dalagatan, L.
tldr: A mixed-methods study of 400 Davao City young professionals finds that digital lending platforms significantly influence debt management behavior, with accessibility, interest rates, and loan purpose as the strongest predictors, while convenience and social influence show unexpected negative relationships.
problem_and_motivation: Digital lending platforms are reshaping borrowing behaviors among young Filipinos, yet limited empirical evidence exists on their specific influence on debt management practices in Philippine urban contexts. There is insufficient understanding of how factors like accessibility, convenience, interest rates, and social influence interact to affect repayment behavior and overall debt management among young professionals in Davao City.
approach: Administered structured self-administered questionnaires to 400 young professionals aged 18-35 in Davao City.
Used stratified sampling across income brackets and employment sectors.
Measured five factors: accessibility, convenience, interest rates, loan purpose, and social influence using 5-point Likert scales.
Analyzed debt management behavior across payment regularity, budget allocation, and borrowing patterns.
Performed multiple regression analysis to determine factor influences on debt management.
Conducted thematic analysis of 20 semi-structured interviews to explore quantitative findings.
Tested reliability using Cronbach's Alpha (0.841) indicating acceptable internal consistency.
Applied construct validity testing using KMO (0.846) and Bartlett's Test (p<0.001).
findings: Digital lending platforms significantly influence debt management behavior among young professionals.
Accessibility is the strongest positive predictor of debt management behavior (β=0.312, p<0.001).
Interest rates significantly influence borrowing decisions and repayment discipline.
Loan purpose clarity correlates with better debt management outcomes.
Convenience shows unexpected negative relationship with effective debt management.
Social influence negatively impacts debt management when it drives uninformed borrowing.
Higher income groups demonstrate more strategic use of digital lending platforms.
Emergency and business purposes show strongest positive relationship with repayment discipline.

topic_relevance.contribution_to_field: This mixed-methods study provides the first comprehensive analysis of digital lending platform efficacy on debt management among young Filipino professionals, demonstrating that accessibility is the strongest predictor of effective debt management while convenience and social influence can negatively impact borrowing behavior. It reveals that higher income groups use digital lending more strategically, and that loan purpose clarity significantly improves repayment discipline, offering insights for platform design and financial literacy interventions.
directly_justifies: Accessibility is the strongest positive predictor of debt management behavior (β=0.312).
Convenience shows unexpected negative relationship with effective debt management.
Social influence negatively impacts debt management when driving uninformed borrowing.
Loan purpose clarity significantly improves repayment discipline.
Higher income groups demonstrate more strategic digital lending platform use.
limits: Geographic limitation to Davao City limits generalizability.
Self-reported data may introduce recall and social desirability bias.
Excludes users without digital lending experience.
topic_relevance.topic_mapping_rationale: The paper was systematically scanned across all 14 topic domains. Domain 5 (Behavioral Profiles) received high relevance for profiling debt management behaviors. Domain 7 (Budgeting/Savings) received high relevance for debt planning and repayment behavior. Domain 4 (Existing Systems) received medium relevance for reviewing digital lending platforms. Domain 10 (Privacy) received medium relevance for data privacy concerns. Domains 1-3, 6, 8, 9, 11, 13, and 14 were considered and rejected as the paper does not focus on Filipino demographics beyond Davao City young professionals, predictive modeling, anomaly detection, mobile design principles, recommendation systems, or synthetic data generation.

remember_this: Accessibility is the strongest predictor of effective debt management among young professionals.
Convenience can negatively impact debt management when enabling impulsive borrowing.
Social influence drives uninformed borrowing that worsens debt management.
Loan purpose clarity significantly improves repayment discipline.
Higher income groups use digital lending more strategically than lower income groups.
